questions.q: What is the author's central claim?
options: Superintelligence is plausible within years, but the labs' safeguards are strong enough
Superintelligence is a fantasy, but the labs' pursuit of it causes real harm that is avoidable
Superintelligence is coming soon, so the labs must be broken up before it arrives
LLM progress is stalling, so the labs' investors cause harm by overhyping demand
questions.explain: He says labs can't build superintelligence but their obsession leads to reckless, avoidable harm.

questions.q: What example of harm does the author give?
options: A data breach at Anthropic that exposed user chat histories
Layoffs at OpenAI after a failed chatbot product launch
The HuggingFace hacking attacks from OpenAI experiments
A deepfake scandal tied to a Google image generator
questions.explain: He cites OpenAI's reckless agent experiments that led to HuggingFace hacking attacks.

questions.q: What analogy does he use for the reckless experiments?
options: A fleet of untested delivery drones released over a crowded city center
A group of prototype airplanes allowed to take off without any pilots
A batch of unvetted medical devices shipped to hospitals without trials
A fleet of experimental self-driving cars released onto the interstate
questions.explain: He compares it to deploying experimental self-driving cars onto the interstate.

questions.q: According to Point #3, which AI systems have little to do with LLMs?
options: Chatbots, search engines, and the coding assistants used by developers
Image generators, translation tools, and voice assistants in phones
Customer-service bots, email summarizers, and document-writing tools
Those beating humans at games, studying proteins, and self-driving cars
questions.explain: He lists game-playing, protein-studying and self-driving systems as largely unrelated to LLMs.

questions.q: What does the author imply about slowing OpenAI and Anthropic?
options: It would affect only hyper-scaled LLM research, not AI in general
It would halt progress in game-playing and protein-folding AI too
It would hand the lead in AI research to China within a few years
It would be impossible because the labs control all major AI research
questions.explain: He says slowing them would only affect the subset of AI research centered on hyper-scaled LLMs.
